note: Legal and review terms that need a plain explanation the first time they appear in Issue, Action, a coverage note, a check's evidence or the Documents not supplied sheet. 'pattern' is a case-insensitive regular expression; 'plain' is the explanation added to the text when the writer has not explained the term. Used by scripts/plain_language.py, validate_review.py and build_review_workbook.py.

terms.plain: an exception written into a clause so that part of it does not apply in a stated case
deducting money one party says it is owed from a payment it owes the other, instead of paying in full
a promise to cover the other party's losses or legal costs if a stated event happens, such as a third-party claim
a clause that sets the most a party can be made to pay for claims under the contract
knock-on losses that do not flow directly from a breach, such as lost profits or lost business
events outside either party's control, such as natural disasters or government action, that excuse delay or non-performance

terms.pattern: cure periods?|right to cure|opportunity to cure
terms.plain: a set time after written notice in which a party can fix a breach before the other may terminate
a serious failure to perform the contract, as opposed to a minor slip
ending the contract early without any breach by the other party, simply because the terminating party chooses to
ending the contract because the other party has breached it
clauses that stay in force after the contract ends, such as confidentiality
a clause saying that if a court strikes out one provision, the rest of the contract still stands
a clause saying the written contract replaces all earlier discussions and promises
transferring a party's rights or obligations under the contract to someone else
replacing a party to the contract with a new one, with everyone's agreement
a promise in the contract that a fact is true or that work will meet a stated standard
a statement of fact made to persuade the other party to sign, which can give a claim if untrue
the country or state whose law is used to interpret the contract
which country's courts or which legal system can hear a dispute
the court or arbitration body where a dispute would be heard
a private dispute process decided by an independent arbitrator instead of a court, usually faster and confidential
taking a dispute to court
legal protection that can limit when a government can be sued, or have a judgment enforced against it, in a court
the government acting as a legal party, here the Government of Canada
giving up a right, either expressly or by not enforcing it
a fixed sum payable for a stated breach, agreed in advance instead of proving the actual loss
a right to take back money already paid if a stated condition is not met
a promise that the client will always get prices at least as good as any other client
terms from a funder or main contract that are passed on to Start2 as a subcontractor
whether a clause binds both parties equally (mutual) or only one of them (one-sided)
separate signed copies of the same contract that together count as one signed agreement
made part of the contract by naming another document rather than copying its text in
treated as true or as having happened, whether or not it actually did
despite; this wording overrides any other clause that says otherwise
in proportion, for example payment for the share of work actually done
not yet earned or used up, for example the part of an advance not yet covered by delivered work
something that must happen before an obligation, such as payment, takes effect
any missed deadline counts as a serious breach that can justify termination
serious or deliberate wrongdoing, usually excluded from liability caps
each party can be held responsible for the whole amount, not just its own share
a promise not to approach or hire the other party's staff, mentors or contacts
a promise to work only with one party, or not with its competitors
a promise not to carry on a competing business
rights in creations such as materials, methods, software, names and logos
permission to use something, such as materials, without owning it
information about an identifiable person; in Singapore its use is governed by the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA)
the opening background statements of a contract, explaining who the parties are and why they are contracting
signed by the parties, so the contract is in force
the other party to the contract
to fix a breach, or the legal right a party has when the other breaches
the client's or a government auditor's right to inspect Start2's records
Start2's list of clauses clients often add, with the position Start2 takes on each
the internal approvals every contract needs: Director of People and Operations, then Regional Director of Innovation and Product Strategy, then CEO
